plans.headline: Wander the garden paths and find the Discovery Garden

main.why: Your toddler can wander the garden paths and find the Charlotte Brody Discovery Garden, stopping wherever something catches {their} eye.
tips: Come early. Parking is paid and often fills before 10 am.
Bring a snack for a bench break halfway through.
Give a two-minute warning, then walk back by a different path.

source.title: Sarah P. Duke Gardens
source.note: Free; paid parking that often fills before 10 a.m. on nice days. Five miles of paths, and the Charlotte Brody Discovery Garden.

alternatives.why: Ride the carousel and the train, then run off extra energy on the playground. It opens at 10 am, so there is no waiting.
tips: Let your toddler pick the first ride.
Snack on a bench before the last ride so leaving goes smoothly.

tips: Let your toddler lead and turn to the next page.

plans.headline: Stroll the arboretum and spot plants up close

main.why: Stroll NC State's garden and let your toddler stop to look closely at plants, leaves and bark along the way.
tips: Let your toddler choose which path to take at each turn.
Bring a snack and have it on a bench before you leave.
Plan a stroller or carrier for tired legs near the end.

source.title: JC Raulston Arboretum
source.note: Free. NC State’s garden; no pets.

alternatives.why: Warm up at Walltown Park, then join Total Tot Time in the gym with a parachute and tunnels to crawl through. A family needs to sign up.
tips: Let your toddler run outside first so the gym feels like a treat.
Bring water and a snack for after the gym.

alternatives.why: An afternoon of carousel and train rides, with the playground for extra running before you head home.

plans.headline: Climb, run and explore the nature trails

main.why: Your toddler can climb on the playground, then follow the greenway to look for sticks, leaves and birds.
tips: Start on the playground, then walk the greenway while {they} still have energy.
Bring a snack and a drink for the picnic shelter.
Walk back toward the car by a favorite spot to make leaving easier.

source.title: Blue Jay Point County Park
source.address: 3200 Pleasant Union Church Road, Raleigh, NC 27614
